chunk_findings.detail: The regression test never creates or enters a Git worktree: `adopted` only does `(repo / ".ddflow").mkdir(exist_ok=True)` and returns the ordinary `repo` fixture. The bug being fixed is specifically `ddflow review` run *from inside a worktree*, but all tests here exercise only a normal adopted repo. If the unfixed code chooses the derived hostname identity only when the repo is a worktree, every assertion in this file can still pass on the unfixed code, so the test does not actually guard B-review-identity-from-worktree-ignores-as-agent.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_review_identity_from_worktree.py:21 (`adopted`)

chunk_findings.detail: `_clean_identity` removes `DDFLOW_AGENT` and `CLAUDECODE` but not `AGENT_NAME`, even though the module doc explicitly calls out `AGENT_NAME` as an identity source that must not be lost. On a machine with `AGENT_NAME` exported, `Ctx.log.agent_id` in `test_detach_argv_redeclares_an_env_sourced_identity` and `test_detach_launches_with_the_resolved_identity` can resolve to the ambient `AGENT_NAME` value instead of the monkeypatched `DDFLOW_AGENT`, causing environment-dependent failures; conversely, no test ever sets `AGENT_NAME`, so a regression on the `AGENT_NAME`-only path (including its leading-dash case) stays green.

chunk_findings.detail: The new `linked` fixture shells out to the real `git` binary via `subprocess.run` (`git commit` and `git worktree add`) instead of going through the git port in `ddflow/adapters`. This violates [r-adapters], which requires git/subprocess tools to sit behind one adapter and says tests should use a fake rather than a subprocess. A test environment that provides the adapter fake but no `git` executable makes `linked` raise `FileNotFoundError` before the identity assertion runs, so the regression test fails for an environment reason rather than testing the fix.

chunk_findings.detail: The `linked` fixture still shells out to the real `git` executable with `subprocess.run` to create the worktree. The prior triage said this is not covered by `r-adapters` because “test setup is not behind it,” but the rule record for [r-adapters] in this review explicitly says external dependencies include git/subprocess tools and that tests use a fake instead of a subprocess. The new test therefore still violates that requirement, and an environment that provides the adapter fake but no `git` executable makes the fixture raise `FileNotFoundError` before the identity assertion runs.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_review_identity_from_worktree.py:44

chunk_findings.detail: The `linked` fixture still calls `subprocess.run([*git, "commit", ...])` and `subprocess.run([*git, "worktree", "add", ...])` directly. This is the previous r-adapters finding still standing at the current lines: the rule says every external dependency (git, subprocess tools) goes through a port in `ddflow/adapters` and that tests use a fake instead of a subprocess. The author’s refutation says test setup is exempt, but the rule text does not exempt test fixtures and explicitly says tests use a fake instead of a subprocess; existing direct-git tests do not waive the rule for this newly added direct `git` call. Concretely, the `git commit` line fails on a machine without ambient git user identity before the worktree scenario is exercised, so the regression test is not hermetic.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_review_identity_from_worktree.py:45-46 [r-adapters]

evidence.note: Re-done at 85c86e1a5; supersedes Rfab9a7de4b's premise. Main already re-declares the resolved identity (8dac8bb72), so the drop it found is fixed there. Remaining failure, probed on a main snapshot: _detach_argv with -dry-run gives ['--agent','-dry-run',...] and python -m ddflow exits 2 'argument --agent: expected one argument'. Reachable: DDFLOW_AGENT resolved '-dry-run' via Ctx; core/agentname.AGENT_NAME allows a leading dash.

Re-checked at 85c86e1a5: no new dependency, one return statement changed in review.py, identity.resolve untouched (r-reuse-core); docstring states why; files under 30 KB (largest 18409 bytes). r-adapters raised by the reviewer on the linked fixture and refuted: the shared repo fixture is real git on purpose (tests/conftest.py docstring).

At 85c86e1a5: _detach_argv emits --agent=<id>; test_review_detach.py assertions updated to that form deliberately; regression test_detach_launches_with_the_resolved_identity[-dry-run] and test_detach_argv_parses_back_to_a_dash_leading_identity read the child's identity through build_parser. Observed: branch 14 passed (both files); main snapshot 5 failed 2 passed, the two dash tests with SystemExit 2 and [sz-dry-run] passing. The other 3 main failures only pin the attached spelling.
roborev job 3997 (agent kilo), roborev review --branch --base main, 4 commits to 85c86e1a5: No issues found; confirmed --agent is a plain store action and the attached value is not read as an option.

roborev job 3997 at 85c86e1a5: no issues; confirmed flag precedence over DDFLOW_AGENT and that the tests are not vacuous. Own grep of ddflow/ for separate-token --agent found 3 other variable-identity sites out of this item's globs: filed as B-agent-separate-token-dash-id.

At 85c86e1a5: ddflow similar on the change: nothing scores 0.5 or more. _detach_argv has one definition and caller; new test file duplicates none; tests/test_review_detach.py pins argv shape, the new file pins parsed identity.

data.summary: The baseline command passes a test file that exists only on the branch (here tests/test_review_identity_from_worktree.py). Replayed on main f8c6444f5: pytest exits 5, "no tests ran", 0 executed. The gate recorded baseline red=false, still_failing=[] and called all 40 failures "new failure(s) not failing on main", while running those same 40 without the branch-only path on main gives 39 failed, 1 passed. A red baseline is hidden and a clean branch is blamed; the verdict is drawn from a run that executed nothing. Fix: drop paths absent from the base, and treat exit 4/5 or 0 tests run as unavailable, never as not failing.
data.title: unit_tests baseline run aborts with no tests ran when the branch adds a test file, so every failure is called new

data.body:
Fixes bug B-baseline-branch-only-test-no-tests-ran: The baseline command passes a test file that exists only on the branch (here tests/test_review_identity_from_worktree.py). The gate recorded baseline red=false, still_failing=[] and called all 40 failures "new failure(s) not failing on main", while running those same 40 without the branch-only path on main gives 39 failed, 1 passed. A red baseline is hidden and a clean branch is blamed; the verdict is drawn from a run that executed nothing. Fix: drop paths absent from the base, and treat exit 4/5 or 0 tests run as unavailable, never as not failing. Found on fix-B-review-identity-from-worktree-ignores-as-agent.

Write the regression test first and watch it FAIL on the unfixed code; then `ddflow complete fix-B-baseline-branch-only-test-no-tests-ran --regression-test <test>` closes the bug with the task (or `ddflow bug fixed B-baseline-branch-only-test-no-tests-ran --regression-test <test>` first).
